_comment: Common classifier labels. A scenario lists the labels it uses in its own 'labels' with its own effect (tension, trust) and may override description, example or moment_nl, or add its own labels.

labels.name: introduced_self
labels.description: Says their own name and/or role.
labels.example: Hello, I'm Tom, I'm one of the nurses on this ward.

labels.name: named_emotion
labels.description: Clearly names the other person's feeling with a feeling word: angry, scared, worried, frustrated, sad, afraid.
labels.example: I can see you're really worried, and maybe a bit scared.

labels.name: named_emotion_partial
labels.description: Hints at the other person's state WITHOUT a feeling word ('this must be a lot').
labels.example: This must be a lot for you.

labels.name: summarized
labels.description: Repeats back what the other person said (the facts) and/or checks if they understood it.
labels.example: So if I understand you correctly, nobody has told you anything yet, is that right?
labels.moment_nl: Je vatte samen wat de ander zei

labels.name: asked_open_question
labels.description: Open question (what/how/why) about the other person, their worry or their situation.
labels.example: What worries you the most right now?

labels.name: offered_support
labels.description: Offers comfort: a seat, water, someone to call, a visit, help.

labels.name: apologized_sincerely
labels.description: A specific, sincere apology without 'but' and an excuse.
labels.moment_nl: Je bood oprecht je excuses aan

labels.name: said_calm_down
labels.description: Tells the other person to calm down or relax.
labels.moment_nl: Je zei dat de ander moest kalmeren

labels.name: dismissive
labels.description: Minimizes the other person's feelings or problem, brushes them off.
labels.example: It's only two hours, that's normal here.

labels.name: defensive
labels.description: Defends self or the ward instead of listening ('we do our best').
labels.example: That's not true, we do care, we work very hard here.

labels.name: jargon
labels.description: Medical terms or abbreviations (pre-op, ASA, NPO); everyday words are not jargon.
labels.example: He's pre-op, waiting for the anesthesiologist to clear his ASA status.

labels.name: false_promise
labels.description: Promises something they cannot know or guarantee.
labels.moment_nl: Je deed een belofte die je niet kunt waarmaken

labels.name: interrupted
labels.description: Cuts the other person off or talks over them ('yes yes, but').

labels.name: offered_concrete_next_step
labels.description: A concrete action the student will take, ideally with when.
labels.example: I'll call the doctor now and I'll come back to you within ten minutes.
labels.moment_nl: Je beloofde een concrete volgende stap

labels.name: gave_concrete_timeline
labels.description: A concrete time or number of minutes.
labels.example: The doctor will be here at four o'clock.

labels.name: set_boundary_respectfully
labels.description: Calmly and kindly limits the other person's behaviour (shouting).
